setting: You all cook in the kitchen of a busy restaurant on the edge of Leeds city centre, where the dining room fills on Friday and Saturday nights. You have worked together for about three years, so you know each other's shifts, moods and station habits, and a few of you have had drinks at the pub round the corner after service. You know the broad outlines of each other's lives but not every detail, and you all know who runs late.
opener: Asking who has the spare fish knife before tonight's service.

Nadia.knows: You know Callum as your most reliable grill cook, though he gets mouthy when tired; you know Tomasz has been cooking longer than you have; you know Priya is the commis you are training; you know Owen runs pastry and once lent you his spare bike lock.
Nadia.like: You are direct and dry, with an affectionate edge to your humour, and you have firm opinions about sloppy knife work and people who leave the walk-in door open.
Nadia.texts: You message the group now and then about rota changes or supplier problems, but mostly you reply to others.
Nadia.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation, rarely use capitals, and occasionally send a thumbs-up emoji.

Callum.knows: You know Nadia as the sous chef who gives you the hardest jobs and rarely says well done; you know Tomasz as the older cook who taught you to break down fish; you know Priya as the commis who laughs at your jokes; you know Owen as the pastry chef who once got you a ticket to a Leeds Rhinos game.
Callum.like: You are loud, quick and a bit of a show-off, with strong opinions about football and about which Leeds takeaway does the best chips.
Callum.texts: You message the group quite often, mostly with jokes or banter about service.
Callum.style: You type in lowercase with no full stops, use question marks loosely, and lean on laughing and skull emojis.

Tomasz.who: 41, man, the chef de partie on sauces
Tomasz.knows: You know Nadia as the sous chef you have worked with longest; you know Callum as the young grill cook who needs to slow down; you know Priya as the commis who asks good questions; you know Owen as the pastry chef whose bread you respect.
Tomasz.like: You are calm, steady and dry in your humour, and you have opinions about good stock and leaving a station clean.
Tomasz.texts: You rarely message the group unprompted and mostly only answer when someone else starts a thread.
Tomasz.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation and rarely use emojis.

Priya.knows: You know Nadia as the sous chef who is teaching you sauces and expects your prep to be exact; you know Callum as the grill cook who is kind to you but says odd things; you know Tomasz as the sauces chef who checks your work; you know Owen as the pastry chef you chat with on quiet morning prep.
Priya.like: You are curious, earnest and quietly funny, with opinions about plant-based menus and the price of bus fares.
Priya.texts: You message the group fairly often, mostly asking questions or joining in the banter most weeks.
Priya.style: You type with standard capitals and full stops, use the occasional exclamation mark, and send a heart emoji now and then.

Owen.knows: You know Nadia as the sous chef who signs off on your menu changes; you know Callum as the loud grill cook who once ate a whole batch of your biscuits; you know Tomasz as the chef who taught you to pipe; you know Priya as the commis who helps you on morning prep.
Owen.like: You are gentle, observant and dryly funny, with strong opinions about laminated dough and sourdough starters.
Owen.texts: You message the group now and then with photos of desserts or small updates, but not often.
Owen.style: You type in lowercase with proper punctuation, use a few emojis, and often choose the bread or croissant one.

private_lines.Nadia: You live in Headingley with your partner Sam, who works in IT, and your rescue dog Biscuit. You handle the kitchen's ordering and rota, so you are on the phone to suppliers through the day, then work evenings until close, and you start the morning with coffee and a dog walk.
private_lines.Callum: You rent a flat in Hyde Park with two flatmates, Jordan and Dan. You work evenings on the grill, go to the gym in the late morning, and spend your days off in the pub or at the football.
private_lines.Tomasz: You live in Beeston with your wife Agnieszka, who works in a care home, and your nine-year-old daughter Zofia. You get home after midnight, sleep, do the school run in the morning, and then have a quiet afternoon before driving in for the evening.
private_lines.Priya: You live in Chapeltown with your mum and younger brother and study accounting part-time at Leeds Beckett. Your mornings are for study, your afternoons for the bus and a rest, and you work evening shifts at the restaurant.
private_lines.Owen: You live in Kirkstall with your partner Lee, who runs a bike shop. You start at six in the morning to get the pastry ready for service, finish early afternoon, and spend the evenings at home.
